record.paper_title: Model Theory of Tame Valued Fields and Beyond: Recent Developments and Open Questions
record.context_brief: Structure of maximal immediate extensions of Q_p(zeta_{p^infty}) and Q_p(p^{1/p^infty})
record.original_question: Let p be a prime. Consider the fields Q_p(zeta_{p^infty}) and Q_p(p^{1/p^infty}), where Q_p(zeta_{p^infty}) is the totally ramified extension of the p-adic field Q_p obtained by adjoining all p^n-th roots of unity (n in N), and Q_p(p^{1/p^infty}) is the totally ramified extension obtained by adjoining a compatible system of p^n-th roots of p (n in N). Both fields, equipped with their unique extensions of the p-adic valuation v_p, are not Kaplansky fields (i.e., they do not satisfy Kaplansky's hypothesis (A) from 1942), and therefore admit uncountably many maximal immediate extensions with distinct elementary L_val-theories, of which uncountably many are not decidable. The maximal immediate extensions that do have decidable elementary L_val-theories (as shown by Kartas 2024) are tame fields. What is the internal valuation-theoretic or algebraic structure of these maximal immediate extensions (beyond the fact that there are infinitely many of them)? What structural properties of such an extension distinguish the decidable ones from the undecidable ones?

evidence.quote: Open problem 2: What is the structure of these extensions (apart from the fact that they are infinite)? What are the indications in their structure that distinguish the decidable from the undecidable extensions?

artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an explicit open question in a recent (December 2025) survey on the model theory of tame valued fields. While Kartas (2024) established that the decidable maximal immediate extensions of these fields are tame, no structural characterisation distinguishing decidable from undecidable maximal immediate extensions of $\mathbb{Q}_p(\zeta_{p^\infty})$ or $\mathbb{Q}_p(p^{1/p^\infty})$ appears in the literature.
